cards.text: Friend, grab an apron, because Genesis 5 opens like a family photo album: "This is the book of the generations of Adam." Adam is the very first man. And page one goes all the way back to the day God created man.

cards.question: On the day God created man, whose likeness did He make him in?
God created them male and female. True or false: right after that, He cursed them.

cards.text: Now jump ahead: Adam is 130 years old when he has a son in his own likeness, after his own image. A brand-new DAD at 130, and I need a nap after one batch!

cards.question: Adam names his new son, born when Adam is 130. What name does he pick?

cards.text: Then the album flips FAST: Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared. Each man has a son and other sons and daughters, lives hundreds of years, and then he died. Adam makes it to 930, Jared makes it to 962, and my phone battery can't make it to lunch.
Next up is Enoch, Jared's son. After he becomes the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years, and I get winded walking to the oven.

cards.question: Every man on the list before Enoch ends the same way: and then he died. True or false: Enoch's life ends that way too.
Enoch walked with God. So what happens to Enoch?

cards.text: Enoch lives a total of 365 years, and then: "Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away." Friend, I got taken away to the back of a junk drawer, and Enoch got taken away by GOD.
Then comes Enoch's son Methuselah, who lives 969 years, and then he died. That's the longest life on this whole list, friend. Imagine the birthday candles. Somebody call the fire department!
Methuselah's son Lamech is 182 years old when he has a son. When he names him, Lamech talks about the labor and toil of their hands.

cards.question: True or false: Lamech says their labor and toil is caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed.
Lamech names his son Noah. What does Lamech hope Noah will do?

cards.text: Lamech looks at baby Noah like he's Friday at five o'clock. Lamech lives a total of 777 years, and then he died.

cards.question: Every dad on this list has his named son somewhere between the ages of 65 and 187. True or false: Noah becomes a father before he turns 100.
After Noah is 500 years old, he becomes the father of three sons. Who are they?

cards.text: Turn the page, friend: men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them. That family album is gonna need a SECOND album.

cards.question: The sons of God see that the daughters of men are beautiful. What do the sons of God do?

answers.text: Take as wives whomever they choose
Wait for the LORD to choose for them
Ask the fathers for their permission

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks. He says His Spirit will not contend with man forever.

cards.question: The LORD says His Spirit will not contend with man forever. What reason does He give?
Then the LORD says that man's days shall be ___ years.

cards.text: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and afterward as well, when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men. And they have children.

cards.question: The sons of God and the daughters of men have children. Who do those children become?

cards.text: And here, friend, the story turns. The LORD looks at man on the earth.

cards.question: What does the LORD see in man that is great upon the earth?
The LORD sees that every inclination of the thoughts of man's heart is altogether ___ all the time.
The LORD sees great wickedness in man. How does the LORD feel about having made man on the earth?

cards.text: The LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart. Then the LORD speaks.

cards.question: The LORD is grieved that He made man. What does the LORD say He will do?

answers.text: Blot out man from the earth

cards.question: The LORD says He will blot out man from the face of the earth. True or false: His words are only about man and leave out the animals and birds.

cards.text: Every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air. And then one little word turns the whole page: however.

cards.question: Noah, however, found ___ in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: "Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD." One man, one line, and that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Genesis 5:1-32 is a genealogy, which is a long stretch. Stop 1 walks through it name by name across 17 cards, and 9 of them are choice cards (cards 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 13, 14, 16, 17) about its details: Seth's name, Enoch, Lamech's naming of Noah, Noah's age and Noah's sons. The doc's own good example for this exact chapter sums up Adam to Noah's sons, including Enoch, in one story card. Genesis 5 should be a single summary story card with no choice cards. Under 'A short passage does what it can. Never force it to fill a stop,' that card can open one stop that also covers Genesis 6:1-8, so no stop is left with only a story card.

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick. The baker should know the stretch is there and what it's about, not memorize it. A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The question says 'right after that,' but Genesis 5:2 only says 'Male and female He created them, and He blessed them.' It gives no timing.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: 'A brand-new DAD at 130' reads as if Seth is Adam's first child. Cain and Abel were born earlier (Genesis 4:1-2).

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. A summary card for a long stretch is still a story card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke compares 'walked with God 300 years' to getting winded walking to the oven. That treats walking with God as physical walking. The core action in the text is a life lived with God, not covering distance, so the comparison doesn't share the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Enoch walked with God. So what happens to Enoch?' makes walking with God the reason he was taken. Genesis 5:24 says 'Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.' The text doesn't say how the two connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in stop 2 are bare retellings with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 3 ('Then the LORD speaks. He says His Spirit will not contend with man forever.'), card 6 (a near-verbatim restatement of Genesis 6:4), card 8 and card 12 all read flat. After card 1, the stop has no humor or personality.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The 'sons of God' (Genesis 6:2) and the 'Nephilim' (Genesis 6:4) appear with no word on who they are. The text leaves their identity open, and interpretations differ.
findings.question: The 'New people' rule says to introduce someone simply the first time they show up, but 'Leave open what the text leaves open' points the other way here. Should Papa Dorin introduce the sons of God and the Nephilim, and if so how? Or should they stay unexplained, leaving the Nephilim to the dictionary pop-up?

findings.problem: The question is the exact wording of Genesis 6:8 with one word blanked ('found ___ in the eyes of the LORD'). Getting it right depends on knowing the wording 'found favor,' not on meaning the baker can reason out from earlier cards.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card opens by repeating Genesis 6:8 word for word, right after card 16 had the baker fill in that same verse. That part is a recap and doesn't move the passage forward.

The 'story isn't over' line ('that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because trust me, this story is NOT done') is nearly a copy of the doc's ✅ example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.').

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
